transcript: Every audience sees, hears and processes information differently. A few simple fixes make your slides work for every viewer, and clearer for everyone.
Low contrast is the most common problem, and one of the easiest to fix. Aim for four and a half to one for normal text, and three to one for large text.
Use near-black text on light backgrounds, put a solid panel behind text on photos, and always test with a checker.
Some viewers can't tell red from green. Give each status a label and an icon, and let colour be an extra cue, not the only one.
Big, plain, left-aligned text reads well in a room and on a small screen. Body text at 24 point or larger, headlines at 36 or larger.
When a deck becomes a video, turn on captions, and let the voice explain what a chart shows, not just say 'as you can see here'.
Accessible slides make better videos. On Pro, AI directs the video, timing animation to your narration. Try Basic first at powerpoint2vid.com.
